hypotheses.claim: Replacing the mandatory serial Retina->materialized-VisualPercept boundary with in-module distributed perceptual state updates reduces perception-to-state latency and state movement without materially reducing task accuracy or replayability.
hypotheses.falsifier: Under matched input and compute, explicit-pipeline baseline has equal-or-lower p95 latency/CPU/state movement, or dissolved mode loses >2 percentage points task accuracy, or cannot reconstruct provenance-complete replay receipts.
hypotheses.best_test: A/B explicit pipeline vs dissolved field on identical Digital Retina features and deterministic fixtures.

hypotheses.claim: Bounded recurrent coupling from world model and memory improves recognition of occluded, ambiguous or context-dependent visual input relative to a feedforward-only perceptual field under matched compute.
hypotheses.falsifier: Feedforward-only field matches or exceeds recurrent condition on difficult perception after controlling parameters/compute, or gains disappear when context information is matched by nonrecurrent post-processing.
hypotheses.best_test: Factorial recurrence x world-model feedback with occlusion, ambiguity and context-swap sets.

hypotheses.claim: High-level visual prediction error/novelty is a better trigger for expensive GWT escalation than fixed-rate full visual reconstruction.
hypotheses.falsifier: Prediction-error trigger misses materially more task-relevant events or costs as much/more than fixed-rate processing at matched downstream utility.
hypotheses.best_test: Event-triggered vs periodic attention with matched salient-event recall and end-to-end action utility.

hypotheses.claim: A hybrid anchor-frame plus change/event fast path dominates both full-frame-only and event-only perception for FRANK's persistent world state.
hypotheses.falsifier: One single-mode baseline Pareto-dominates hybrid mode in accuracy, missed events, latency and compute across representative workloads.
hypotheses.best_test: Three-way periodic full frame vs change-only vs hybrid anchor+change benchmark.

hypotheses.claim: Making perceptual hypotheses first-class Clay state and preserving multiple alternatives until evidence/context settles them reduces premature misclassification on ambiguous scenes.
hypotheses.falsifier: Single-best-label baseline has equal/better calibration and lower error without increased correction cost, or multi-hypothesis state creates unstable/expensive oscillation.
hypotheses.best_test: Ambiguous/bistable/occluded benchmark comparing forced early label vs set-valued alternatives.

hypotheses.claim: World-model feedback must be precision-bounded; otherwise dissolved perception increases prior-induced false positives/hallucination-like errors.
hypotheses.falsifier: Unbounded/strong top-down feedback does not increase false positives under misleading priors/no-signal conditions relative to bounded precision controls.
hypotheses.best_test: Misleading-prior x sensor-quality factorial with no-signal and unknown-object controls.

hypotheses.claim: If the perceptual field pre-integrates persistent world/memory state, the Clay-native 4B model can achieve equal task utility with less model-visible visual/context payload than caption/image-heavy baselines.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched 4B tasks require equal or greater model-visible tokens/bytes/latency for equal accuracy and calibration.
hypotheses.best_test: Same 4B fixture across raw/caption, explicit VisualPercept and bounded perceptual-assembly projections.

hypotheses.claim: Putting sensor ingress and perceptual fast path into the H3 one-module process reduces IPC/serialization overhead enough to improve sensor-to-action latency on project hardware.
hypotheses.falsifier: External-process and in-process topologies are equivalent within measurement noise or one-module mode worsens p95/p99 latency, crash recovery or resource contention.
hypotheses.best_test: Same device/fixtures through out-of-process vs in-process ingestion with trace-level timing.

counterhypotheses.claim: The explicit Retina module is already a good abstraction; dissolving it mostly removes observability/modularity and yields little performance benefit.
Benefits attributed to recurrent perception are reproducible by simpler late contextual reranking or post-processing.
Persistent world-state coupling causes error propagation and stale priors that outweigh context benefits.
The main bottleneck is the physical vision model/kernel, so process/module consolidation cannot materially change end-to-end latency.
A distributed PerceptualField is harder to train/debug than a typed VisualPercept boundary and increases implementation complexity without cognitive gain.

promotion_rule: Owner-fixed architecture target may guide implementation, but performance/cognitive claims remain OPEN until differential Harness evidence exists. Negative results remain first-class.
